artworks.title: The Rape of Europa
artworks.description: Titian's late poesie sends Europa over the waves on Zeus' bull, her companions stranded on the shore — the Phoenician princess's abduction as Venetian colour and terror. Oil on canvas, Isabella Stewart Gardner Museum, Boston.

artworks.title: The Abduction of Europa
artworks.description: Rembrandt's rare mythological oak panel stages Ovid's bull-ride with a Dutch landscape behind it: Europa mounted, her attendants crying out as Zeus carries her toward Crete. J. Paul Getty Museum, Los Angeles.

artworks.title: The Rape of Europa
artworks.description: Rubens copies and recharges Titian's invention for the Spanish court: Europa's white flesh against the dark bull, putti and sea spray framing the ride that founds Crete. Oil on canvas, Museo del Prado, Madrid.

artworks.title: The Rape of Europa
artworks.description: Reni's cool Bolognese classicism sets Europa on the bull against a clear sky — the abduction as poised, almost serene motion, commissioned for Władysław IV Vasa. National Gallery, London (Mahon loan).

artworks.title: The Rape of Europa
artworks.description: Young Goya paints Europa's bull-ride with Rococo lightness — the Phoenician princess still aloft on Zeus, the myth that named a continent restaged for an eighteenth-century Spanish wall.

artworks.title: Zeus as a bull carries off Europa (Ovide moralisé)
artworks.description: Ovide moralisé (Rouen, MS O.4, f. 71): Jupiter, in the shape of a white bull, carries Europa off across the sea.

artworks.title: Europa and the bull (Veroli Casket, ivory relief)
artworks.description: Lid of the Veroli Casket (London, Victoria and Albert Museum, 216-1865), carved in Constantinople: Europa carried off on the bull, among centaurs, maenads and erotes dancing to a lyre.

music.title: Europa riconosciuta
music.description: Salieri's opera for the opening of La Scala returns Europa of Tyre — once Zeus' lover — to reclaim her name and settle a Phoenician throne war.

popCulture.title: Europa (moon)
popCulture.description: Jupiter's ice moon keeps the princess beside the god who carried her — Europa orbiting Zeus under another name.

popCulture.title: Europa series
popCulture.description: The euro banknote redesign takes her name and a Hellenistic vase portrait — the princess as the face of a currency, not a film about the bull.
